content: 1. Amlodipine is a dihydropyridine calcium channel blocker that inhibits the transmembrane influx of calcium ions into vascular smooth muscle and cardiac muscle cells. 2. It selectively inhibits calcium ion influx across cell membranes, with a greater effect on vascular smooth muscle cells than on cardiac muscle cells. 3. 4. The contractile processes of cardiac and vascular smooth muscle depend on the movement of extracellular calcium ions into these cells through specific ion channels, which amlodipine inhibits. 5. Experimental data suggest that amlodipine binds to both dihydropyridine and nondihydropyridine binding sites. 6. Negative inotropic effects can be detected in vitro, but such effects have not been observed in intact animals at therapeutic doses. 7. Serum calcium concentration is not affected by amlodipine. 8. Amlodipine is an ionized compound (pKa = 8.6) within the physiologic pH range, and its interaction with calcium channel receptors is characterized by a gradual rate of association and dissociation, resulting in a gradual onset of effect. 9. The precise mechanisms by which amlodipine relieves angina are not fully delineated but are thought to include reducing total peripheral resistance (afterload) and myocardial oxygen demand during exertion. 10. Amlodipine has been shown to block constriction and restore blood flow in coronary arteries and arterioles in response to calcium, potassium, epinephrine, serotonin, and thromboxane A2 analog in experimental animal models and human coronary vessels in vitro. 11. This inhibition of coronary spasm is responsible for the effectiveness of amlodipine in vasospastic (Prinzmetal's or variant) angina. 12. Amlodipine tablets are formulated as white tablets equivalent to 2.5 mg, 5 mg, and 10 mg of amlodipine for oral administration. 13. In addition to the active ingredient, amlodipine besylate, each tablet contains inactive ingredients such as microcrystalline cellulose, dibasic calcium phosphate anhydrous, sodium starch glycolate, and magnesium stearate. 14. 15. 16. Chronic once-daily oral administration maintains antihypertensive effectiveness for at least 24 hours. 17. Plasma concentrations correlate with effect in both young and elderly patients. 18. 19. 20. In hypertensive patients with normal renal function, therapeutic doses of amlodipine decrease renal vascular resistance and increase glomerular filtration rate and effective renal plasma flow without changing filtration fraction or proteinuria. 21. Amlodipine does not change sinoatrial nodal function or atrioventricular conduction in intact animals or humans. 22. In clinical studies, amlodipine therapy did not alter electrocardiographic intervals or produce higher degrees of AV blocks in angina patients. 23. After oral administration of therapeutic doses, absorption produces peak plasma concentrations between 6 and 12 hours. 24. Absolute bioavailability has been estimated to be between 64% and 90%, and the presence of food does not alter its bioavailability. 25. Amlodipine is extensively metabolized in the liver, with about 90% converted to inactive metabolites and 10% of the parent compound and 60% of the metabolites excreted in the urine. 26. Approximately 93% of the circulating drug is bound to plasma proteins in hypertensive patients. 27. Elimination from the plasma is biphasic, with a terminal elimination half-life of about 30–50 hours. 28. Steady-state plasma levels are reached after 7 to 8 days of consecutive daily dosing. 29. The pharmacokinetics of amlodipine are not significantly influenced by renal impairment, allowing patients with renal failure to receive the usual initial dose. 30. Elderly patients and those with hepatic insufficiency have decreased clearance of amlodipine, resulting in an increase in AUC of approximately 40–60%, necessitating a lower initial dose. 31. A similar increase in AUC was observed in patients with moderate to severe heart failure. 32. Amlodipine has been evaluated for safety in more than 11,000 patients in U.S. and foreign clinical trials, and treatment was generally well-tolerated at doses up to 10 mg daily. 33. Most adverse reactions reported during therapy were of mild or moderate severity. 34. The most common side effects are headache and edema. 35. Amlodipine therapy has not been associated with clinically significant changes in routine laboratory tests, including serum potassium, serum glucose, total triglycerides, total cholesterol, HDL cholesterol, uric acid, blood urea nitrogen, or creatinine. 36. Amlodipine has been used safely in patients with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, well-compensated congestive heart failure, coronary artery disease, peripheral vascular disease, diabetes mellitus, and abnormal lipid profiles. 37. Amlodipine is extensively metabolized by the liver, and its plasma elimination half-life is prolonged in patients with impaired hepatic function, necessitating slow titration in such patients. 38. Amlodipine should be used during pregnancy only if the potential benefit justifies the potential risk to the fetus. 39. It is not known whether amlodipine is excreted in human milk, and nursing should be discontinued while amlodipine is administered. 40. 41. Clinical studies did not include sufficient numbers of subjects aged 65 and over to determine whether they respond differently from younger subjects. 42. Elderly patients have decreased clearance of amlodipine, resulting in an increase in AUC of approximately 40–60%, and a lower initial dose may be required. 43. Amlodipine is not significantly removed by hemodialysis due to its high protein binding. 44. 45. If hypotension occurs, cardiovascular support, including elevation of the extremities and judicious administration of fluids, should be provided. 46. 47. Amlodipine is a long-acting calcium channel blocker formulated as the besylate salt, chemically described as 3-Ethyl-5-methyl (±)-2-[(2-aminoethoxy)methyl]-4-(2-chlorophenyl)-1,4-dihydro-6-methyl-3,5-pyridinedicarboxylate monobenzenesulphonate. 48. Its empirical formula is C20H25ClN2O5·C6H6O3S, and it is a white crystalline powder with a molecular weight of 567.1. 49. Amlodipine is slightly soluble in water and sparingly soluble in ethanol. 50.
